title: Odd-homology vanishing conjecture for moduli spaces of planar trivalent graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a planar trivalent graph, and let $\mathcal{M}(G)$ be the moduli space of admissible decorations of $G$: each edge $e$ is assigned a point $D(e)\in\mathbb{CP}^2$, and at every vertex the decorations on the three incident edges are pairwise orthogonal. For an integer $i$, write $H_i(\mathcal{M}(G))$ for the $i$-th homology group of this moduli space.

**Odd-homology vanishing conjecture.** For any planar trivalent graph $G$ and for $i$ odd, one has

$$
H_i(\mathcal{M}(G))=0.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by an earlier conjecture cited in the source. The source does not establish the vanishing for all planar trivalent graphs.
source_name: ZIpei Zhuang, “Tait coloring and a moduli space”, arXiv:2111.10567 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.10567

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).
